candidate_sentence_map.S1: AS Tallinna Sadam’s revenue increased 2.4% year on year to EUR 59.3 million in the six months ended 30 June 2026, but profitability declined substantially.
candidate_sentence_map.S2: Operating profit fell 25.7% to EUR 13.6 million, reducing the operating margin from 31.6% to 22.9%.
candidate_sentence_map.S3: Adjusted EBITDA decreased 13.5% to EUR 25.8 million, with its margin declining from 51.5% to 43.5%.
candidate_sentence_map.S4: Profit before income tax fell 27.3% to EUR 11.4 million, while profit for the period declined 41.7% to EUR 6.0 million, or EUR 0.02 per share compared with EUR 0.04 a year earlier.
candidate_sentence_map.S5: Revenue growth was mainly supported by a EUR 0.9 million increase in charter-fee revenue, as icebreaker Botnica recorded 130 charter days versus 110 in the comparative period, including a 20-day North Sea project in June.
candidate_sentence_map.S6: Electricity sales rose EUR 0.6 million, helped by higher sales volumes, market prices, new network tariffs introduced in March and a security-of-supply fee resulting from a regulatory change.
candidate_sentence_map.S7: Ferry-service revenue increased EUR 0.3 million due to tariff indexation and compensation for additional Regula trips.
candidate_sentence_map.S8: These gains were outweighed by a 24.0% increase in operating expenses to EUR 20.2 million.
candidate_sentence_map.S9: Fuel costs rose 47.6% to EUR 4.4 million because of higher diesel prices and more severe ice conditions, which increased ferry fuel consumption.
candidate_sentence_map.S10: Electricity costs increased 28.8% to EUR 3.1 million, while technical maintenance and repair expenses rose 80.0% to EUR 2.8 million.
candidate_sentence_map.S11: The latter increase reflected more extensive repairs to Botnica, ferries and harbour infrastructure, while the previous year included a EUR 0.9 million insurance indemnity for Botnica repairs.
candidate_sentence_map.S12: Depreciation, amortisation and impairment increased 6.0% to EUR 12.9 million, partly due to the commissioning of a new quay and capitalised ferry dry-docking projects.
candidate_sentence_map.S13: Operating volumes weakened: cargo declined 5.0% to 6.5 million tonnes, mainly because liquid bulk fell 33.8%, while passengers decreased 2.0% to 3.6 million and vessel calls fell 4.8%.
candidate_sentence_map.S14: Helsinki passenger traffic was affected by the scheduled dry-docking of Eckerö Line’s Finlandia.
candidate_sentence_map.S15: The report also links lower liquid-bulk volumes and higher fuel costs to geopolitical conditions, including Russia’s war in Ukraine and the US-Iran conflict and Strait of Hormuz blockade.
candidate_sentence_map.S16: The comparison was further weakened by EUR 0.9 million of profit from the 2025 Rail Baltica land sale and other prior-year benefits.
candidate_sentence_map.S17: Lower net finance costs, down 11.2% to EUR 2.3 million, partly mitigated the operating decline.
candidate_sentence_map.S18: The Group paid EUR 19.2 million in dividends, resulting in a EUR 4.4 million reduction in cash to EUR 27.6 million and operating cash flow of EUR 18.2 million, down from EUR 26.3 million.

evaluation.label: Generally yes
evaluation.justification: K1, K2, K3, and K4 are fully covered with supporting details in the candidate. K7 is partially present, covering the Botnica project, Regula trips, and dividend payment, but missing the Tallinn City Council plan adoption and the OP Corporate Bank loan agreement. K5 (investment details), K6 (balance sheet items), and K8 (market capitalisation and share price data) are entirely missing. The summary captures most high-importance financial performance drivers and profitability changes, but lacks several medium/high importance items, resulting in a 'Generally yes' assessment.
